summary:
FSD (Supervised) is a subscription in the U.S.: Tesla lists $99 a month and no longer sells it outright [2][3]. Tesla reported 1.74 million active FSD subscriptions at the end of Q3, counting earlier lifetime purchases, and the fleet passed 17 billion supervised miles this week [4][31].

The current software is still FSD v14.3.13 on AI4 cars and v14.3 Lite on HW3; 2026.38.5.11 is the most widely installed build and a 2026.38.5.12 point release carrying the same FSD began appearing on November 4 [1][19][27]. HW3 still won't get unsupervised FSD, and Tesla's target for unsupervised FSD in owners' cars is Q2 2027, inside Robotaxi zones first [5][6].

Robotaxi added Fort Worth on November 2, its seventh city, and service hours now run 6 a.m. to 2 a.m. [28]. Federal crash reports list 26 Tesla robotaxi incidents in Austin since July 2025 [25].

In Europe, the Dutch regulator approved changes that cut the system's maximum speed margin over the limit from 50% to 10% and name it Tesla Assisted Driving on screen; EU-wide approval is still pending [29]. Tesla's new referral program pays FSD owners a free month or a $99 credit per referral, up to 12 a year [30]. In South Korea, a consumer group is taking Tesla to the Fair Trade Commission over selling FSD on cars that can't legally use it [32].

price.purchase: Can't be bought outright: Tesla says FSD (Supervised) is subscription-only [2]. The $8,000 one-time purchase ended after February 14, 2026 [3].
price.note: FSD bought outright by an earlier owner stays with the car unless it was transferred away before March 31, 2026; a previous owner's subscription does not carry over, and Luxe Package FSD may carry over depending on when it was bought [2].

versions.note: 2026.38.5.11 began rolling October 24 and is the most widely installed build; 2026.38.5.12, with the same FSD, appeared on November 4 [19][27]. Rewritten AI compiler, vision-encoder upgrades and Automatic Collision Evasion [1]. In Europe, AI4 cars run FSD 14.2.2.6 in 2026.39.6 [27]. Tesla's manuals now call this computer SI4 [21].

Distilled from v14 for HW3: parking, unparking, reversing, Arrival Options and Speed Profiles, including a new SLOTH profile; carried in 2026.38.5.11 and the November 4 point release 2026.38.5.12 [1][19][27].

hardware.fsd: None as built: HW2 is not FSD capable [13].
hardware.note: HW2 went into S and X from October 2016 to about August 2017; S/X built earlier in 2016 have the older Autopilot 1 hardware and no FSD path [13].

hardware.fsd: None as built; runs FSD (Supervised) only if the computer was retrofitted to HW3, which Tesla did free for owners who had bought FSD [13].
hardware.note: HW2.5 from about August 2017 to March 2019; 2017 is a split year with HW2. Check the Autopilot computer line in Additional Vehicle Information [12][13].

hardware.note: HW3 from March 22, 2019 [13]; 2019 is a split year with HW2.5 and 2023 a split year with AI4 (cars bought after March 2023 likely AI4) [12].

check: In the car: Controls > Software > Additional Vehicle Information shows the Autopilot computer (2.5, 3 or 4); this needs software 2024.38 or later [12].
Controls > Software also shows whether Full Self-Driving Capability is in the car's included package [2].
Front cameras: AI4 cars show two red lenses and one black dummy lens; AI4 side repeaters have a red tint [12].
Build date: S/X after about March 2023, U.S. Model Y after late May 2023 and the 2024 Model 3 are likely AI4 [12].
Tesla's owner's manuals now call the computer the "SI Computer": HW3 is listed as SI3 and AI4 as SI4. Same hardware, new name [21].
transfer: You can no longer move FSD to another car or account: Tesla's FSD (Supervised) Transfer Program ended on March 31, 2026 [2][3]. If you sell a car whose FSD was bought outright, the purchase stays with that car, so the next owner gets it [2]. If you had a subscription, it ends with your ownership and the buyer must subscribe on their own Tesla account [2]. There is no current transfer offer. The new referral program is not a transfer: subscribers get a free month and outright owners a $99 Tesla credit for each referral who subscribes, up to 12 a year, in app 4.62 or later [30].

robotaxi.status: No one on board; Cybercabs in the fleet; geofence expanded to Circuit of the Americas for the Grand Prix [9][14]; NHTSA reports list 26 Tesla robotaxi crashes in Austin since July 2025 (25 Model Y, 1 Cybercab) [25]. Texas registrations: 1,080 robotaxis, 573 of them Cybercabs, not all in service [24]
No one on board; Tesla says Cybercab rides start in Dallas this month [6][14][28]
No one on board [14]; on October 26 the zone grew from about 25 to an estimated 254 square miles, by third-party trackers' count [23]
Launched November 2 at 6 a.m.; the zone runs west of downtown to TCU and White Settlement and along I-820 toward Saginaw [28]; reported as unsupervised [33]
Safety driver required by California rules; not driverless [5][7]

robotaxi.place: Las Vegas, Phoenix, Jacksonville, San Antonio
robotaxi.status: Announced as coming soon; no dates. Tesla says San Antonio is next [7][8][28]

buying: Check Controls > Software for Full Self-Driving Capability: only an outright purchase stays with the car [2].
Don't count on moving FSD from your old car; transfers ended March 31, 2026 [2].
Prefer AI4: HW3 gets the Lite build and won't run unsupervised FSD [1][5].
On a 2017-2019 S/X or early Model 3, confirm the computer is HW3 or later, not HW2/HW2.5 [12][13].
Budget $99 a month if the car has no purchased FSD [2].
Outside the U.S., don't buy a car with an aftermarket FSD unlock: Korean police booked 80 people for using such devices, which carry up to two years in prison there [26].
Selling a car with purchased FSD? It stays with the car, so price it in; a referral reward is not a way to move it [2][30].
changes: Robotaxi launched in Fort Worth on November 2, Tesla's seventh city; service hours are now 6 a.m. to 2 a.m. [28][33].
Netherlands' RDW approved changes for Europe: maximum speed margin cut from 50% to 10%, reset to 0% at every start, and the name Tesla Assisted Driving on screen; EU-wide approval still pending [29].
FSD referral program live: a free month (subscribers) or $99 credit (owners) per referral, up to 12 a year [30].
Update 2026.38.5.12, with FSD v14.3.13 and v14.3 Lite, appeared on November 4; 2026.38.5.11 remains the most installed build [27].
The fleet passed 17 billion miles on FSD (Supervised), about 6.76 billion of them in cities [31].
A Korean consumer group is filing a Fair Trade Commission complaint over FSD sold for about $6,726 on cars that can't legally use it [32].

pt.summary:
O FSD (Supervised) é uma assinatura nos EUA: a Tesla cobra US$ 99 por mês e não vende mais a compra definitiva [2][3]. A Tesla informou 1,74 milhão de assinaturas ativas no fim do 3º trimestre, contando compras vitalícias antigas, e a frota passou de 17 bilhões de milhas supervisionadas nesta semana [4][31].

O software atual continua sendo o FSD v14.3.13 nos carros AI4 e o v14.3 Lite no HW3; a 2026.38.5.11 é a versão mais instalada e uma atualização 2026.38.5.12, com o mesmo FSD, começou a aparecer em 4 de novembro [1][19][27]. O HW3 não terá FSD sem supervisão, e a meta da Tesla para o FSD sem supervisão nos carros de clientes é o 2º trimestre de 2027, primeiro dentro das zonas de Robotaxi [5][6].

O Robotaxi chegou a Fort Worth em 2 de novembro, sua sétima cidade, e agora funciona das 6h às 2h [28]. Relatórios federais registram 26 incidentes com robotáxis da Tesla em Austin desde julho de 2025 [25].

Na Europa, o regulador holandês aprovou mudanças que reduzem a margem máxima acima do limite de velocidade de 50% para 10% e dão ao sistema o nome Tesla Assisted Driving na tela; a aprovação em toda a UE ainda está pendente [29]. O novo programa de indicação da Tesla dá aos donos de FSD um mês grátis ou US$ 99 em crédito por indicação, até 12 por ano [30]. Na Coreia do Sul, um grupo de consumidores vai à Comissão de Comércio Justo contra a venda do FSD a carros que não podem usá-lo legalmente [32].

de.summary:
FSD (Supervised) ist in den USA ein Abo: Tesla verlangt 99 Dollar im Monat und verkauft es nicht mehr dauerhaft [2][3]. Tesla meldete Ende des dritten Quartals 1,74 Millionen aktive FSD-Abos, frühere Käufe eingerechnet, und die Flotte hat diese Woche 17 Milliarden überwachte Meilen überschritten [4][31].

Aktuell bleibt FSD v14.3.13 auf AI4-Autos und v14.3 Lite auf HW3; 2026.38.5.11 ist der am weitesten verbreitete Stand, und ein Update 2026.38.5.12 mit demselben FSD tauchte am 4. November auf [1][19][27]. HW3 bekommt kein unüberwachtes FSD, und Teslas Ziel für unüberwachtes FSD in Kundenautos ist das zweite Quartal 2027, zuerst in Robotaxi-Zonen [5][6].

Robotaxi startete am 2. November in Fort Worth, der siebten Stadt, und fährt jetzt von 6 bis 2 Uhr [28]. Bundesunfallberichte verzeichnen seit Juli 2025 26 Vorfälle mit Tesla-Robotaxis in Austin [25].

In Europa hat die niederländische Behörde Änderungen genehmigt, die den maximalen Spielraum über dem Tempolimit von 50 auf 10 Prozent senken und das System auf dem Bildschirm Tesla Assisted Driving nennen; die EU-weite Zulassung steht noch aus [29]. Teslas neues Empfehlungsprogramm gibt FSD-Besitzern pro Empfehlung einen Gratismonat oder 99 Dollar Guthaben, bis zu zwölfmal im Jahr [30]. In Südkorea zieht eine Verbrauchergruppe wegen des FSD-Verkaufs an Autos, die es nicht legal nutzen dürfen, vor die Fair Trade Commission [32].
